patterns_found.visual_evidence: The desktop sketch shows a compact input-like box in the top-right header area, visually separated as a search field/control.
patterns_found.behavior_notes: Should support text entry and search submission; may expand, submit on Enter, or trigger a results page depending on implementation.
patterns_found.ambiguities: The sketch does not show whether results are live/autocomplete or simple submit-only search.

patterns_found.visual_evidence: The mobile sketch lacks visible full navigation while the desktop sketch clearly includes a left navigation rail, implying that navigation is likely collapsed behind a mobile toggle.
patterns_found.behavior_notes: A mobile nav trigger should reveal/hide the site navigation or section menu that is persistently visible on desktop.
patterns_found.ambiguities: No explicit hamburger icon is drawn in the mobile sketch, so the exact trigger placement and whether it opens a drawer, overlay, or inline panel is unclear.

patterns_found.visual_evidence: The inferred mobile navigation toggle and the desktop search control both imply interactive widgets that need managed keyboard focus; cross-viewport navigation changes also suggest focus handling when menus open/close.
patterns_found.behavior_notes: When the mobile menu opens, focus should move into the revealed navigation and return to the trigger on close; keyboard access for search and any revealed navigation states should be preserved.
patterns_found.ambiguities: Focus behavior is not directly depicted because no explicit open state is shown in either sketch.

sketch_notes: The sketches imply a mostly content-driven page with low JavaScript complexity. The strongest explicit interaction is a desktop header search field. The main cross-viewport implication is responsive navigation: desktop exposes a persistent left-side menu while mobile suppresses it, strongly suggesting a collapsed mobile navigation toggle even though the icon is not explicitly drawn. No clear evidence appears for tabs, accordions, modals, dropdowns, sticky behavior, or dynamic loading.
